parole.significato: honorific address on an adult male; mister, sir, efendi
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish افندی, from Byzantine Greek ἀφέντης (aphéntēs), from Ancient Greek αὐθέντης (authéntēs), from αὐτο- (auto-) + *ἕντης (*héntēs) + -της (-tēs).
From Ottoman Turkish دونوم (dönüm) belonging to دونمك (dönmek, “to turn”), presumably a calque from Byzantine Greek στρέμμα (strémma, “stremma”, literally “that which is turned”).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish فرچه (fırça), فورچه (furça), from Byzantine Greek βρούτζα (broútza), from Vulgar Latin *bruscia, a Germanic borrowing, equalling German Bürste.

parole.significato: cloths wrapped around an infant, “baby roll”, swaddling-clothes
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish قونداق (kundak, “bundle, faggot; rifle butt”), from Byzantine Greek κοντάκιον (kontákion), diminutive of Byzantine Greek κόνταξ (kóntax, “pole”), diminutive of κοντός (kontós, “pole”).

Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish مغازه (mağâza), borrowed from Byzantine Greek μαγαζίον (magazíon), borrowed from Venetan magazén, borrowed from Arabic مَخَازِن (maḵāzin), from مَخْزَن (maḵzan), from خَزَنَ (ḵazana).
